questions.question: Name the five functions of the skeleton.

points.text: Support, protection, movement, mineral storage, blood cell production.

questions.question: How many bones make up the axial skeleton?

points.text: 80 bones make up the axial skeleton.

questions.question: Give one example each of a long bone, a short bone, a flat bone and an irregular bone.

points.text: Long: femur; Short: carpals; Flat: cranium; Irregular: vertebrae.

questions.question: Explain why the vertebral column is classified as irregular bones.

points.text: Vertebrae have complex, irregular shapes that do not fit into the long, short, or flat categories. Each vertebra has a body, spinous process, transverse processes and a vertebral foramen, making their shape irregular.

questions.question: Which part of the vertebral column supports the most body weight, and why?

points.text: The lumbar region (5 vertebrae) supports the most body weight because it bears the entire weight of the upper body and transfers it to the pelvis and legs.

questions.question: Describe how the skeleton supports blood cell production.

points.text: Red bone marrow, found in the sternum, ribs, pelvis, vertebrae and the ends of long bones, produces red blood cells (carry oxygen), white blood cells (fight infection) and platelets (help blood clot).
